ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier (CMF), Articles L.561-1 to L.561-50 and R.561-1 to R.561-62, as amended by Ordonnance n° 2020-115 du 12 février 2020 transposing Directive (UE) 2015/849 (4AMLD) and Directive (UE) 2018/843 (5AMLD); beneficial ownership register (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs, RBE) governed by Article L.561-46 CMF and Articles R.561-50 to R.561-57 CMF, operationalised by Décret n° 2017-1094 du 12 juin 2017 and Décret n° 2019-1129 du 31 octobre 2019; Loi n° 2016-1691 du 9 décembre 2016 (Sapin II); SAS vehicle under Articles L.227-1 et seq. and L.123-32 du Code de commerce; regulated investment services subject to Articles L.532-9, L.541-1 et seq. CMF and the Règlement Général de l'AMF (portfolio management company and financial investment adviser regimes) with ORIAS registration.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (authorities — Tracfin, DGFiP, customs, AMF, ACPR and AML-obliged entities — hold unrestricted access to the RBE; restricted legitimate-interest disclosure to journalists, civil-society associations and researchers under Décret n° 2019-1129)
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_ownership_threshold_rules: A beneficial owner is any natural person who, directly or indirectly, holds more than 25% of the share capital or voting rights of the SAS. Where no natural person is identifiable at the 25% threshold, the law pierces through intermediate legal vehicles and, failing identification, treats the senior managing director (président) and all shareholders acting jointly as deemed beneficial owners for AML purposes (Article L.561-2-2 CMF).
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_piercing_doctrine: Substance over form: chains of intermediate companies, trusts, foundations and foreign partnerships are iteratively aggregated; economic ownership, joint control and bearer-share structures are re-characterised on the basis of genuine control and economic benefit rather than mere share registry entry; UBO declarations for the RBE must be certified accurate by the legal representative and are verified by the greffier and Tracfin.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official Companies Registry in the corporate shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or French Consular Legalization where the origin State is not a Hague party

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the board or shareholder resolution authorising incorporation of the French SAS and the capital contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary or notary of the corporate shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or French Consular Legalization in respect of the origin State

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds/source-of-wealth statement for the capital contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or French Consular Legalization according to the origin country's certification practice

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Police clearance certificate (extrait de casier judiciaire equivalent) for each proposed director, président and compliance officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent judicial or public prosecutor authority in the person's country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified French translation of every non-French document in the bundle

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original documents retain Apostille or legalization; the translator's sworn certification accompanies the French text

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation and continuous screening of all shareholders, UBOs, officers and authorised signatories against (i) the UN Security Council Consolidated List (Resolutions 1267/1988/2253), (ii) the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List including Regulation (UE) n° 269/2014 and Regulation (CE) n° 2580/2001, (iii) the French national asset-freeze arrangements administered by the Direction générale du Trésor, (iv) the OFAC SDN List, which is mandatory given the USD custody-wire and SWIFT interbank payment rails, and (v) Interpol Red Notices and adverse-media repositories. PEP determination follows Article L.561-10 CMF and FATF Recommendation 12: automatic enhanced due diligence, senior-management approval, documented source-of-funds and source-of-wealth verification for every engagement with a PEP or PEP-linked UBO; records retained at least five years after business relations end (Article L.561-20 CMF).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), administered by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI), in conjunction with the Registre National des Entreprises (RNE), the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via infogreffe.fr, and the ORIAS register for regulated financial advisers.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered name must be in Latin script and, under Loi n° 94-665 du 4 août 1994 (loi Toubon), commercial documents must contain a French-language version of any foreign-language name; the name must not infringe registered trademarks (Article L.711-2 du Code de la propriété intellectuelle) or create confusion with an existing RCS-registered entity (Article L.123-32 du Code de commerce), and must not be contrary to public order or good morals.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On rejection, the applicant shall (1) obtain the written refusal with its stated grounds from the INPI/guichet unique or the competent greffe; (2) file within one month a recours gracieux with the same authority, attaching supporting documentation including trademark coexistence certificates, apostilled corporate consents, or an amended name proposal; (3) where the conflict rests on a third-party trademark or an existing RCS name, negotiate a coexistence/renunciation letter or file a nom modifié through formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; (4) in the absence of resolution, lodge a judicial appeal before the juge commis à la surveillance du Registre du commerce et des sociétés within two months of the refusal; and (5) for regulated tokens such as Banque or Société de gestion de portefeuille, obtain the prior ACPR/AMF or ORIAS clearance and annex it to the refiled application; the name reservation, where separately granted by the greffe, may be extended once for a further 30 days upon reasoned request and payment of the greffe fee.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code, Articles L. 227-1 to L. 227-14 concerning simplified joint-stock companies
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: French Commercial Registry (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés - RCS) of the Commercial Court
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Act of Incorporation and Articles of Association
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital of one euro (€1), fully paid-up with no escrow account requirement for private SAS
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The Board of Directors of [Entity Name], a French Société par Actions Simplifiée, met on [Date] at the registered office. The directors unanimously resolved as follows: (1) to subscribe to the entire initial share capital amounting to one euro (1 EUR), represented by one hundred (100) shares of one cent (0.01 EUR) each, fully paid up; (2) to adopt the registered office at [full address]; (3) to appoint [Director 1] as President, [Director 2] as Chief Executive Officer, and [Director 3] as Director. The resolution further authorizes the President to execute all necessary documents and formalities with the registry. Signed by all directors present.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Signing of Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public or guichet-entreprises.fr online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare detailed articles including capital, corporate object, registered office, directors' powers. All shareholders sign the acte constitutif. Notarize the document if required by law.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Submit amended documents within 15 days if queried by registry

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Online portal guichet-entreprises.fr or direct submission to RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload electronic copy of acte constitutif and statuts, pay any nominal fees if applicable, request SIREN number and extract Kbis. Complete formalities within 30 days.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Procedural amendment or resubmission if application is queried

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP), administered locally through the Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE). Tax accounts and filings are generally managed through the DGFiP professional portal, impots.gouv.fr. Company formation and registration formalities are filed through the national business formalities portal operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI), formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A French SAS is registered through the INPI business formalities portal. Upon registration, it receives a SIREN identification number and a SIRET for each establishment, recorded in the Registre national des entreprises and generally also in the Registre du commerce et des sociétés. The competent SIE handles corporate tax and VAT account activation. A French VAT number consists of the prefix FR, a two-digit control key, and the SIREN. A foreign taxable person without a French establishment applies to the DGFiP for VAT registration before carrying out transactions requiring French VAT reporting; a non-EU business generally appoints a French fiscal representative unless an applicable statutory exception or mutual-assistance arrangement applies. EU-established businesses are generally not required to appoint a representative but may need a French tax representative or agent for procedural purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A SAS is generally subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS). A qualifying newly created SAS may elect temporary partnership-style taxation under Article 239 bis AB of the French Tax Code, generally for up to five fiscal years, subject to ownership, activity, age, size, and other statutory conditions. This is not a U.S.-style check-the-box election. No general hybrid-mismatch election changes a SAS's French tax classification; anti-hybrid rules may deny deductions or require income inclusion in applicable cross-border arrangements.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT; taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover threshold applies to a French-established taxable business that must charge VAT: registration and liability depend on the nature and location of taxable transactions. Eligible small businesses may use the franchise en base de TVA. For 2025, the principal domestic thresholds are generally EUR 85,000 for sales of goods and accommodation and EUR 37,500 for services, with higher tolerance thresholds generally EUR 93,500 and EUR 41,250, respectively; statutory eligibility and activity-specific rules must be checked. Non-established businesses generally do not benefit from a domestic turnover threshold for taxable transactions requiring French VAT registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is implementing domestic B2B electronic invoicing and e-reporting in phases. Under the enacted timetable, all businesses must be able to receive electronic invoices from 1 September 2026; large and intermediate-sized businesses must issue them from that date, while SMEs and micro-enterprises must issue them from 1 September 2027. Domestic B2B invoices must use an authorized platform or the public invoicing portal under the applicable system. E-reporting applies to specified transactions, including relevant B2C and cross-border transactions. France does not generally require real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping of every invoice. Businesses must comply with statutory invoice-content, retention, and transmission requirements.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods from France to destinations outside the European Union may be exempt with credit (effectively zero-rated) under the French VAT rules implementing Article 262 of the EU VAT Directive, provided the goods are dispatched or transported outside the EU and the exporter retains reliable evidence of export. Intra-EU supplies are governed by separate rules and are not exports for this purpose. Services are not automatically zero-rated as exports: the place-of-supply rules determine whether French VAT applies. A supply to a non-EU business may be outside the scope of French VAT under the general B2B rule, subject to exceptions; services connected with French immovable property and other special-category services may remain taxable in France. Input VAT recovery depends on the applicable deduction rules and substantiation.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export customs declaration and proof of exit from the EU customs territory, including the export accompanying document or electronic exit confirmation where available
Commercial invoice identifying the parties, goods, value, and relevant VAT treatment
Transport evidence appropriate to the route, such as a bill of lading, air waybill, CMR consignment note, or carrier proof of delivery
Purchase order, contract, and correspondence supporting the export transaction and the identity of the customer
Proof of payment where relevant to substantiate the transaction; an inward remittance certificate is not a generally prescribed French VAT export document
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France imposes no general statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline of 180 days for export proceeds. Export exemption claims may be denied or reversed if the taxpayer cannot establish that the goods left the EU or that the transaction satisfies the applicable conditions; resulting VAT, late-payment interest, and penalties may be assessed. Under the French Tax Code, penalties can include a 40% increase for deliberate breach and an 80% increase in specified cases of fraudulent activity or abuse, in addition to statutory interest; the applicable assessment depends on the facts and procedure. False documents or fraudulent conduct may also trigger criminal liability.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (BdF) and the European Central Bank (ECB) under the French Foreign Exchange Control regime administered jointly with the Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury). The legal framework is codified in the French Monetary and Financial Code (CMF, Book V).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible for both current and capital account items, in line with Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU). For French resident entities, cross-border transactions with non-residents must be reported to the Banque de France for balance-of-payments statistical purposes. Profit remittance, dividend distribution, loan repayment, and liquidation proceeds may be freely transferred abroad provided the origin of funds is documented and banks file any necessary declarations to TRACFIN (French FIU). There are no exchange controls, but the flow of physical currency, asset transfers, and payments exceeding certain thresholds require administrative declarations to customs or tax authorities.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France imposes no statutory timeline, mandatory conversion ratio, or surrender requirement for export proceeds. Exporters may retain EUR or foreign currency balances in with any authorised bank or financial institution. Nonetheless, under EU Regulation 184/2005 (transposed by the Banque de France), all payment receipts from non-residents must be reported for balance-of-payments statistics via the resident bank. Specific direct-investment inflows and outflows above €15 million per annum must be reported quarterly; no foreign-exchange conversion or repatriation is mandated for goods, services, or intangibles.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Société Générale (Kleinwort Hambros for Private Banking)
Crédit Agricole CIB (LCL for Domestic Branch)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Medium for consolidated operational payments and foreign-currency collection, but Low for capital escrow, custody, or investment-settlement accounts. Legal constraints under ACPR and the E-Money Directive (2009/110/EC): EMIs cannot grant credit, hold client securities, or provide portfolio-management services. For an MFO with discretionary investment advisory activity, EMIs must not substitute for a licensed investment firm; they may be used only as a payment-rail interface, with mandatory safeguarding of funds in a low-risk account at a credit institution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote account opening is theoretically permitted for standard low/medium-risk entities, but for a multi-family office (classified as High_Risk_Special_License under French AML/CTF rules) Tier-1 banks will impose enhanced due diligence. In practice, at least one natural-person statutory director (Président, Directeur Général, or authorised signatory) must attend an in-person or live video-conferencing interview at a French branch (for non-resident directors, a consular-notarized passport and apostilled ID may be accepted). The bank retains discretion to require a physical meeting for non-resident UBOs or when the economic substance cannot be verified through documentary evidence alone.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk business classification: 'Discretionary Portfolio Advisory for Multiple Private Client Families' (NAICS 523920), which is a regulated financial-activity (Conseiller en Investissements Financiers / Démarcheur) requiring AMF registration or exemption.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid AMF registration certificate as a CIF (Conseiller en Investissements Financiers) or a written legal opinion confirming an express family-office exemption from MiFID licensing; complete AML/CFT manual; UBO declaration (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) with detailed source of wealth and source of funds; list of intended client families and their tax/practical residences.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex beneficial-ownership structure with foreign fiduciary layers, trusts, or foundations among non-resident directors/investors.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Organisation chart certified by a legal counsel; copies of trust deeds, foundation articles, or other constitutive documents with apostille; government-issued IDs and address proofs for all UBOs (natural persons above 25%); sworn declarations of independence and professional references for money managers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border inward capital injection from a non-EU jurisdiction, particularly from high-risk third countries (e.g., tax havens, jurisdictions subject to FATF/EU money-laundering blacklist).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original or digitally signed capital-contribution deed (acte de souscription) filed at the French Trade Registry; recent 12-month bank statements of the remitting entity and beneficiary; source-of-funds letter certified by the remitting entity's auditor; confirmation of no ongoing criminal/tax investigations in the remitter's jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential presence of short-lived corporate form (e.g., SAS newly incorporated within less than 12 months) or rapid changes of shareholding/management.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full tax and legal due-diligence report on the SAS's incorporation chain; ordinary and extraordinary minutes of shareholder and board meetings; a certified business plan with projected cash flows, custody arrangements, and client onboarding SOPs; professional indemnity insurance evidence (RC Professionnelle) with coverage commensurate with portfolio sizes.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For injection from a shareholder resident inside the European Union, use SEPA Credit Transfer (ISO 20022) with remittance information containing the purpose code 'DASI / Direct Investment Contribution' (mirroring OECD Balance-of-Payments classification). For an extra-EU remitter, use SWIFT MT103 with field 23B 'CRED', field 70 containing the shareholder capital contribution description (e.g., 'Souscription au capital social de l'entité SAS / Registration Capital'), and field 72 including the Banque de France statistical-form reference (e.g., 'R2/3'). Prior to receipt, the French Bank must be provided with the notarized capital subscription agreement, company Kbis excerpt, UBO declaration, and source-of-funds evidence. The payment must be cleared to a domestic French euro account held in the same legal entity name; if the injection is inbound from a sanctioned jurisdiction, automatic freeze and TRACFIN reporting may occur.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For settlements on investment purchases or operational charges (fees, taxes, professional liabilities) within the euroarea, use SEPA CT with remittance references and, where required, the tax-royalty purpose code. For non-euro disbursements (e.g., in USD, GBP, JPY) or securities settlements through custodial banks, use SWIFT MT103/MT202 COV with proper beneficiary-bank and intermediate-bank identifiers. For import of goods or services under a documentary credit, a French issuing bank will open a Commercial Letter of Credit under the ICC UCP600 (e.g., SWIFT MT700 for issuance, MT720/MT730 for amendments and MT747 for reimbursement confirmation). Multi-family office portfolio trades typically require free-of-payment (FOP) delivery through the central securities depositories (Euroclear France, Clearstream) with cash legs via UCITS/Payment vs Payment (PvP) mechanisms; the bank's custody and treasury desk must be nominated before onboarding.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: OATC-OFF-EXCHANGE FX SPOT: Daily spot FX trades through a licensed French credit institution, not subject to margin requirements under EMIR.
OUTRIGHT FX FORWARD: OTC forward contracts (e.g., EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/JPY) used for locking conversion rates on expected inflows/outflows; counterparty must be an ACPR/EU-authorised bank.

NON-DELIVERABLE FORWARDS (NDFs): Permissible for volatile non-EMU currencies (e.g., CNY, INR, KRW) when a deliverable forward is unavailable; cleared via the French bank's offshore desk and subject to ISDA documentation.

FX CURRENCY SWAP: Fixed-to-fixed and floating-to-fixed, used for hedging long-term balance-sheet FX exposure; must be reported to a registered trade repository under EMIR and may require initial-variation margin posting if entered with a non-EU counterparty.

CURRENCY OPTIONS (OTC/EXCHANGE-TRADED): Purchased through an ACPR-licensed broker-dealer, or cleared through LCH.Ltd (a recognised central counterparty), with arrangement under the AMF French derivative-frequency threshold framework.

CROSS-CURRENCY INTEREST RATE SWAP (CCIRS): Used to hedge long-term capital injections and foreign-currency borrowings, subject to the same EMIR trade-reporting, clearing obligation regulator-vs-bilateral, and where required, margining protocol (AANA threshold conditions must be monitored).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of annual accounts (dépôt des comptes annuels) with the Commercial Court Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (jurisdiction of registered office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of fiscal year-end for shareholder approval, then within 1 month of approval for filing; for calendar FY ending 31 Dec: approval by 30 Jun, filing by 30 Jul.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing injunction, compulsory filing under court order, fines up to €7,500 for the legal entity and €1,500 per director, and risk of administrative strike-off from RCS leading to dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Declaration of beneficial owners (Déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs) in case of shareholding changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (RCS file)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of any change in beneficial ownership; annual internal verification with no change filing required if unchanged.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine up to €10,000 for the legal entity and €2,000 for natural person; repeated non-filing can trigger RCS strike-off or judicial liquidation proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholders' decision (approval of accounts and allocation of income) held and registered in the minutes book
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company records at registered office (must be available for inspection by Greffe and tax authorities)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of fiscal year-end (e.g., by 30 June for a 31 Dec fiscal year); minutes recorded in the register of decisions.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance does not trigger direct fine but invalidates accounts filing and exposes the company to late-filing penalties and legal liability of the president for breaches of corporate governance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory appointment of a statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) if the SAS exceeds two of the following thresholds at FY-end: total assets > €4,000,000, net turnover ex-VAT > €8,000,000, average workforce > 50; mandatory audit also required if the SAS controls one or more subsidiaries exceeding specified thresholds or upon voluntary request of shareholders.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général) per ANC Regulation 2016-07, as amended; IFRS permitted for consolidated accounts; individual accounts must comply with French accounting standards.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No standalone annual UBO filing exists under French law; however, the company must maintain an accurate register of beneficial owners and file updates to the Greffe within 30 days of any change. The board must annually review the register (typically at the annual meeting) and record confirmation in the minutes to satisfy AML obligations.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Decisions and Minutes (Registre des décisions de l'associé unique)
Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 400 - 2,500 (typical annual fee for French registered virtual office/legal proxy services)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 4,000 - 12,000 (typical fee for a small multi-family office entity with mandatory or voluntary audit)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 15% reduced rate on first €42,500 of taxable profit for SMEs; R&D tax credit (up to 30% of eligible expenses); innovation status benefits

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IS liasse fiscale declaration via impots.gouv.fr electronic portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 15th day of the third month following fiscal year-end (e.g., 15 May for 31 December year-end)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net turnover for the fiscal year
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: N/A for French resident SAS; report consolidated group turnover if applicable

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after deductions and incentives

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: €750 minimum to €7,500 maximum or 0.5% of tax due per month of delay (max 25%) + 0.2% monthly interest on unpaid tax

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 12.8% on dividends paid to non-resident shareholders (treaty relief to 5% or 0% for portfolio dividends)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Submit Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) and relevant forms via impots.gouv.fr or specific declaration to reduce WHT rate
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 25% statutory reduced by treaty to 0-10%; Interest: 25% statutory reduced by treaty to 0-10%

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: €50 million consolidated revenue for local file; €750 million for master file
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Limited applicability under French DAC6 and ESR for holding or IP entities; pure advisory services generally do not trigger full ESR

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to file corporate tax return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-submission of annual IS declaration by deadline
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fine €750-€7,500 or 0.5% of tax per month late (max 25%) plus interest; possible criminal prosecution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors jointly and severally liable for tax debts; possible imprisonment for willful non-compliance or fraud

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using non-arm's length pricing without documentation or adjustment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalties up to 80% of understated tax or more; restitution of tax plus interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal civil and criminal liability; possible disqualification from management

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax evasion penalties: fines up to 500% of tax evaded, imprisonment up to 5 years
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Imprisonment, fines, and personal restitution obligations

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating or maintaining entities without economic substance for tax avoidance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization of transactions; penalties up to 80% of tax; criminal sanctions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability for tax, possible jail time for fraudulent conduct
